name: Coinbase
look: Full-bleed dark heroes with floating product cards, one blue used scarcely, and editorial pill geometry with no sharp corners.

hero.title: The trusted place to buy and hold
hero.sub: Regulated custody, audited reserves and a fee schedule you can read before you sign up. Built for holding, not for churning.

features.title: Custody first, trading second
features.sub: Most people want to buy something and still own it in five years. That is the product this is built around.

items.title: Qualified custody
items.body: Assets held under a qualified custodian arrangement, segregated and bankruptcy-remote.

items.title: Audited reserves
items.body: Holdings attested quarterly by an independent auditor, with the report published.

items.title: Simple buying
items.body: Buy, hold and sell without a trading interface, at a fee stated before you confirm.

items.title: Advanced trading
items.body: A full order book with limit and stop orders for people who want one.

items.title: Self-custody wallet
items.body: Move to a wallet you control, with the keys never touching our infrastructure.

items.title: Learn
items.body: Plain explanations of what you are buying, including the ways it can go wrong.

showcases.title: Boring, on purpose
showcases.body: Ninety-eight percent of assets sit offline in geographically distributed cold storage with multi-party signing. The remainder is insured. None of that is exciting, which is the point.

showcases.title: Custody an auditor will accept
showcases.body: Segregated, bankruptcy-remote accounts with attestation reports issued directly to your auditors, plus same-day settlement in eight fiat currencies.

gallery.title: LEARN
gallery.sub: What you are buying, and how it can go wrong.

testimonial.quote: The learn pages explain how you can lose money. I have never seen another platform in this industry lead with that, and it is why I trusted the rest.
testimonial.name: Sarah Lindqvist

tiers.name: Simple
tiers.desc: Buy and hold without an order book.

items.a: Assets are held by a regulated custodian in segregated, bankruptcy-remote accounts — legally separate from the company's own balance sheet.

items.q: Are fees really shown before I confirm?
items.a: Yes, as a currency amount on the confirmation screen, not a percentage you have to compute. The spread is included in that number.

items.q: Can I move assets to my own wallet?
items.a: Yes, at any time, with the self-custody wallet or any external address. Withdrawal is not gated behind a support conversation.

items.q: What happens if the company fails?
items.a: Customer assets are segregated and bankruptcy-remote, which means they are not available to creditors. The legal structure is described in full on the custody page.

cta.title: Start with what you understand
cta.sub: Regulated custody, audited reserves, and fees stated up front.

footer.tagline: The trusted place to buy and hold.

notes: A single blue carries every primary CTA, the wordmark and inline brand links — and it is used scarcely.
Display weights stay modest at 400, never heavy. The restraint is the trust signal.
Editorial pill geometry throughout: pills for CTAs, circles for asset glyphs, generous rounding on cards. No sharp corners anywhere.
The strongest signature is a full-bleed dark hero with floating product-UI cards composited over it.
Trading semantics are text colour only — green up, red down — and never a background fill.
